races.name: Smarter Gambling Starts At gambling.com Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Chico Dulce
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator in solid AW form — has won at 8f on Standard Lingfield and a step up to 10f looks well within range; Billy Loughnane in the saddle is a positive and this horse's five-race same-going record (2 wins, 5 placed) is the most compelling surface profile in the field.

runners_data.name: Shifra
runners_data.note: Recent win and place over 10f on Good going is promising, but only two runs on similar going and a note of fading in finishes is a real concern; genuinely a rear-of-field closer in nature, and with the map already crowded in the hold-up zone, getting clear at the business end on a 14-runner card is far from assured.

runners_data.name: Arlecchino's Rex
runners_data.note: Strong AW profile with 15 runs on Standard going (1W, 6P) and Cieren Fallon's booking adds positive intent — he is a natural closer who will be working from deeper than ideal given the crowded midfield, but his consistency at this trip and surface marks him as a genuine each-way participant.

runners_data.name: Moonlit Cloud
runners_data.note: Returned from just 8 days ago and has placed at 12f on Standard Lingfield, which is encouraging; a natural hold-up runner asked to slot into midfield in this big field, and the hood (p) suggests he can be tricky — his recent course placing at a longer trip is the primary asset here.

runners_data.name: Dubai Harbour
runners_data.note: Has a win and multiple places on Standard AW going across 6f-12f trips and handles the surface, but three of his last five runs have seen him finish mid-division or worse; a natural closer whose best chance depends on the pace collapsing late rather than being able to find his own rhythm at the rear.

runners_data.name: Stacey Racey
runners_data.note: Four of six recent runs at 7f-8f — today's 10f trip is a genuine question mark; she has placed at this distance before, but her AW record (0W, 3P from 11 runs) and the compression of hold-up horses into the midfield make her difficult to recommend with confidence.

runners_data.name: Crazy Plan
runners_data.note: The only realistic prominent companion to Roman Secret and the key pace dynamic variable — if he presses the front-runner the whole race shape changes; his recent second over 12f on Standard AW suggests he stays the trip well and Jason Watson will know his tactical importance at the head of affairs.

runners_data.name: Lady Aiyana
runners_data.note: Tongue strap noted and a mixed recent record with a string of mid-division finishes at trips up to 12f — six of her last nine runs on similar going have produced a single place, and being a genuine hold-up type asked to race out of position in a 14-runner field does her no favours.

runners_data.name: Summer Evening
runners_data.note: Tongue strap worn and a deeply unremarkable recent profile — a 21st, an eighth and a ninth among her last five runs paints a bleak picture; she is a natural closer who will struggle to assert from a compromised midfield position in a field this size.

runners_data.name: Warriors Choice
runners_data.note: Lengthy absence at 70 days and a sequence of 8-8-8-5-4 suggests consistent underperformance; Tom Dascombe's yard has a decent 14-day strike rate (1/12) so there may be stable intent, but a natural hold-up runner with no wins on Standard AW going is hard to enthuse about in this shape.

runners_data.name: Warrnambool
runners_data.note: 228 days off the track is the headline concern — returning from seven months away into a competitive 14-runner handicap is a big ask; has placed at 10f on Standard AW before and Luke Morris is an experienced pilot to reintroduce him, but the fitness question is unavoidable.

runners_data.name: Lady Of Chivalry
runners_data.note: Only three career runs on record with a single placed effort — very limited profile to assess; tongue strap worn and handles Standard AW going but no evidence yet of the class or experience to compete in a field this deep.

runners_data.name: Roman Secret
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner with the licence to dictate — won over 10f on Standard AW last time and Finley Marsh can simply slot him into an uncontested lead; STYLE_FIT tag acknowledges he is mapped slightly forward of natural comfort, but in this field he is the obvious shape-setter and holds the tactical initiative throughout.

runners_data.name: Little Tiger
runners_data.note: AW form has exclusively come on Good or similar soft surfaces with only 2 from 15 runs on similar going — the surface profile is the stand-out concern; a natural hold-up type who has never won on Standard Lingfield and may find conditions conspiring against him at this trip.

races.paceDynamic: Roman Secret is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-strong field and should stride into an uncontested lead from the off, setting a sustainable gallop on Lingfield's AW straight mile-and-a-quarter. Crazy Plan is the only other runner with a prominent style, meaning Roman Secret faces no serious pace pressure and can control tempo entirely on his own terms. The field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up types — Warriors Choice, Shifra, Arlecchino's Rex, Dubai Harbour, Stacey Racey, Summer Evening, Lady Aiyana, Moonlit Cloud and others are all natural rear-pacers compressed into the midfield mapping because there are simply too many closers for the race to accommodate at the back. With one front-runner setting a measured, unforced pace and a wall of hold-up horses who cannot all get their natural position, this race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or just off the pace and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — horses forced to come from the true rear will face a test of getting through traffic on a track that rewards those able to travel with the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Roman Secret Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Roman Secret leads from the break and Crazy Plan settles in behind without pressing for the front.
scenarios.body: Roman Secret sets a controlled, uncontested tempo throughout, conserving enough to quicken off the home turn and hold on as the closers arrive too late; this is a Lingfield AW shape that strongly suits the horse who controls fractions. Crazy Plan, tracking in second, is best placed to challenge in the straight and has recent course form at the trip to underpin a bold showing.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If Roman Secret sets a strong enough gallop that he ties up inside the final furlong and the backmarkers find a clear run.
scenarios.body: Chico Dulce and Arlecchino's Rex, both proven on this surface and at this trip, would be the primary beneficiaries of a late collapse in front; Arlecchino's Rex has strong AW form figures and handles Standard Lingfield well. Chico Dulce has won here over 8f on identical going and a step up to 10f may unlock further improvement.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle Out
scenarios.trigger: If Crazy Plan pushes Roman Secret for the lead early and a contested pace develops.
scenarios.body: A more honest gallop set by two prominent runners opens the door for horses tracking just off the pace such as Arlecchino's Rex to take advantage; the front pair would likely weaken in the final furlong having burned more energy than either wants. This shape marginally widens the winning scope but still demands proximity to the pace, not a deep hold-up run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Blindsides Field
scenarios.trigger: If the large field of 14 causes crowding on the home turn and pace collapses mid-race, rewarding horses who find daylight.
scenarios.body: With so many redistributed hold-up types crammed into midfield, a bunched field and checked momentum could allow a fortunate escapee to coast through; Warrnambool's long absence (228 days) makes him speculative, but his AW form across the trip has placed before. Lady Of Chivalry and Little Tiger lack the profile for this, but an unusual shape could flatter a fresh runner in a muddled race.

watchPoints.text: Roman Secret — if Finley Marsh gets a clean break and is allowed to stride clear unchallenged, he controls all fractions and the race is set up entirely on his terms; monitor whether Crazy Plan attempts to press him in the first three furlongs.

Crazy Plan — Jason Watson's early positioning is the key variable: if he tracks Roman Secret closely rather than sitting in behind, a contested pace develops and the entire race shape shifts away from the front-runner and toward the closers.

Midfield traffic — with 14 runners and at least eight genuine hold-up types compressed into midfield, watch for horses checking or getting blocked on the home turn; Arlecchino's Rex and Chico Dulce both need a clear passage from two furlongs out and any interference will cost them materially.

Warrnambool — 228 days off the track; monitor paddock condition and early market moves, as a well-backed returning runner would shift the probability weight toward Scenario D or B if connections signal strong confidence.

Moonlit Cloud — returned just 8 days ago and wears the hood (p); a horse who raced so recently in a 14-runner field can sometimes come out fresh and sharp, making Robert Havlin's early positioning worth tracking from the stalls.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 British EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Desert Sands
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Ismail Mohammed & Jose Santos who has shown a tendency to fade in the finish — a concern in a 5f race where early energy must be rationed; 32 days off and a disappointing recent form string (6-0-9) suggest confidence is not at its highest.|

runners_data.name: Birkacre Brow
runners_data.note: High OR of 120 makes her the class standout on paper and James Tate's yard has hit form (4/11 in 14 days); drops back to 5f after two runs at 6f, which could sharpen her finish, and Billy Loughnane is an elite claimer capable of positioning her ideally off Ouragan's pace.|

runners_data.name: Ouragan
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in this field, Archie Watson's filly has placed twice on Standard AW going and returns just 12 days after her last run in good heart; Luke Morris can dictate a controlled gallop and the absence of any rival willing to seriously challenge for the lead is her primary tactical advantage.|

runners_data.name: Bellatina
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's filly carries strong recent place form over this 5f trip — twice second on Good and once on Firestone — and Cieren Fallon is a high-quality booking; however, she naturally wants to race prominently and with two other horses ahead of her for the front positions, she is likely to be squeezed into a midfield berth that blunts her effectiveness.|

runners_data.name: Crimson Blaze
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's hold-up filly arrives on an 11-day turnaround with modest recent form (5-6-8-6) and has gone winless across four attempts; her true closer's profile is the least well-suited to a controlled Ouragan-dictated tempo on a flat AW track that rarely suits deep hold-up tactics over 5f.|

races.paceDynamic: Ouragan is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to dispute the lead, Luke Morris can control tempo from the outset at a sustainable, measured gallop over this flat Lingfield AW 5f. Desert Sands and Birkacre Brow will press forward from their prominent positions and apply some presence behind the leader, but neither is expected to force Ouragan into a gruelling early duel. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure their natural position — Bellatina is a genuine prominent racer by style but is mapped to midfield here because Desert Sands and Birkacre Brow are both likely to occupy the positions close to Ouragan, leaving Bellatina shuffled back against her natural inclinations. A controlled, front-runner-friendly shape with a fair but unhurried tempo favours Ouragan and any prominent horse capable of tracking the leader comfortably — true hold-up horses chasing from the rear face an uphill task if the pace never truly stretches the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ouragan Controls, Front Runs Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Ouragan is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead and dictates a sustainable gallop throughout
scenarios.body: Morris settles Ouragan in front without pressure and the modest tempo means no dramatic late collapse, allowing the leader to find more in the closing stages. Prominent horses who track smoothly are next best, but none can manufacture the pace to haul Ouragan back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Reels In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Desert Sands or Birkacre Brow maintain relentless pressure that drains Ouragan in the final furlong
scenarios.body: Sustained proximity racing robs Ouragan of the breather that makes a front-running display sustainable, and a prominent chaser with a stronger finish nips past late. Birkacre Brow's superior OR of 120 gives her the class edge in this scenario if she travels kindly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Bellatina Overcomes Poor Position
scenarios.trigger: If Bellatina, despite being pushed back from her natural prominent berth, finds a clear run and produces a strong late burst
scenarios.body: Racing out of role from midfield, Bellatina would need gaps to open in a small five-runner field and a stronger-than-expected pace to bring her finishing effort into play. Her sim-going record and recent placed form on similar surfaces give her an outside chance, but the style mismatch is a meaningful handicap.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce on Slow Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically and the hold-up horse Crimson Blaze arrives with a sustained late run
scenarios.body: Crimson Blaze is a genuine hold-up type who needs the race to be truly run to suit, and a slow tempo over 5f on AW makes that highly unlikely to materialise. Finley Marsh would need the front runners to fade badly, which is improbable when Ouragan can control tempo without being pressed.

watchPoints.text: Ouragan's ability to get a clean break from the stalls is critical — if she is slow away, Desert Sands or Birkacre Brow could steal the lead and completely alter the race shape.|

Birkacre Brow's class advantage (OR 120 vs a field top-rated at 79 excluding her) is significant and Billy Loughnane may elect to sit just off Ouragan's shoulder rather than allow a comfortable lead, which would pressure the pace more than expected.|

Bellatina's redistribution to midfield means her jockey Cieren Fallon may try to manufacture a forward position at the break — watch the early exchanges for a scrimmage as prominent types jostle for position in a small field.|

Desert Sands has faded in her last three finishes at 6f and now drops to 5f; if the pace is modest her early speed could see her last better, but her form string of 6-0-9 makes her a risk rather than an opportunity in a pace-tracking role.|

Crimson Blaze's hold-up style in a five-runner field on a flat AW track is structurally disadvantaged — watch whether Finley Marsh opts to push her forward early to avoid being left too far detached in what may be a slowly-run small-field sprint.|

races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Pomme Pomme
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Jack Channon, has finished placed at 10f on Good but her AW sim-going record reads just 1 win from 14 appearances — suspect stamina once pace bites; Rose Dawes takes off a useful 5lb but this mare's record in competitive handicaps is inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Radiance
runners_data.note: George Boughey's three-year-old returns after a massive 326-day absence having won her sole AW start over 7f; stepping up sharply to 1m2f is the key question, and Billy Loughnane's booking on a lightly-raced filly with a 137-form string hints at trainer confidence despite the layoff.

runners_data.name: Distant Shore
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's filly has been placed five times in her last five starts with a win thrown in, showing admirable consistency but a habit of finding one too good; Robbie Downey rides and the hood (headgear) is noted — she races prominently and the 1m2f AW trip should be within range of her 8f best on Good.

runners_data.name: Big Bear Hug
runners_data.note: The lone genuine hold-up horse in the field, Pat Cosgrave's partner won over 11f on AW Standard and has the profile of a horse who benefits when the pace is brutal; at 7 years old Jim Boyle has him fit (29 days), and his sim-going record (4/15) shows he consistently picks up ground late without always converting.

runners_data.name: Asset
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's three-year-old is the most recently active of the front-runners, winning last time out at 8f on Good; the AW sim-going record is tight (1/5) but she is stepping into a bigger race fresh off a win — Prescott does not do that without confidence, and Luke Morris knows this horse well.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Athene
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly has won twice and placed twice in her last five runs showing excellent recent form; she is a natural prominent racer whose position on the pace map has been shifted back because the front and prominent slots are oversubscribed — her STYLE_FIT of 0.83 reflects that she will struggle to express her best if denied her preferred position behind the pace.

runners_data.name: Guesstimate
runners_data.note: William Haggas has a filly with a win over this course and trip on Good last time out; she is inherently a prominent-tracking type whose map position was adjusted to midfield because of front-runner congestion — Cieren Fallon will need luck through traffic, and the STYLE_FIT of 0.93 means her chance is only marginally compromised if she gets any cover early.

runners_data.name: Rastnet
runners_data.note: David Egan's mount carries top weight of 142lbs and has an excellent AW record — six places from nine sim-going runs including a win — with the 59-day break manageable for a horse that has been placed fresh before; headgear (p) noted, and his stamina over 10-12f is proven, making him a clear beneficiary if the three-way pace duel burns off the leaders.

runners_data.name: Deedaydiva
runners_data.note: Alan King's filly arrives on 94 days off and her only AW start produced an 8th over 8f on Good, so there are unresolved questions about both the surface and the step to 1m2f; Luke Catton claims 3lb and her best form (1-3 in last five) has come on softer ground, raising fitness and going concerns on Standard AW.

runners_data.name: She Commands
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old has two wins from four AW starts including at this course and trip, making her the most course-savvy front-runner in the field; freshened after 53 days, her sim-going record (2 wins from 4) is strong, and if Edward Greatrex can control the lead without being drawn into a prolonged duel, she is the most dangerous pace-setter here.

races.paceDynamic: She Commands, Pomme Pomme, and Asset are all confirmed front-runners, guaranteeing a strong gallop from the off over Lingfield's 1m2f AW trip — there is no realistic chance of a false pace here. The three will fight for early supremacy, compressing the prominent contingent (Radiance, Distant Shore, Rastnet, Deedaydiva all wanting to race close) into a dangerous pack 2-3 furlongs out where traffic is near-certain. That sustained pressure will stretch the field and filter out anything without genuine stamina, with the finishing straight likely to reward those who have either conserved energy behind the scrum or who hold enough class to sustain the tempo. This race shape strongly favours genuine hold-up horses and true stayers who can thread through late, or one standout front-runner with the class to dictate rather than scrap — the field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred position, with She Commands (class, course form) and Asset (recent winning form, Sir Mark Prescott placement) most likely to actually lead, pushing Spirit Of Athene and Guesstimate — both natural prominent types — into roles they are not built for.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other off and only the most durable stayer survives the sustained gallop.
scenarios.body: She Commands, Pomme Pomme, and Asset press each other throughout, the pace remains unrelenting, and the race becomes a test of raw stamina from the 3f pole home; a horse with proven staying ability who settles close to the pace without scrapping for it is ideally placed. Runners who can track without overcommitting early — Rastnet, Big Bear Hug — are best suited as the leaders are neutralised by their own pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Class Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the confirmed leaders — most likely She Commands — establishes a clear advantage early and controls tempo to suit herself.
scenarios.body: She Commands has two wins at this course and trip on Standard and is freshened up after 53 days; if she finds a comfortable lead without a prolonged duel, Ralph Beckett's filly can bowl along at a controlled clip and have enough left to repel late challengers. Asset is the alternative if She Commands is headed early, as Sir Mark Prescott's placing of a returning winner rarely lacks confidence.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Type Weaves Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace-battle implodes mid-race creating a gap that a prominent runner tracking just off the scrum can exploit.
scenarios.body: Distant Shore and Radiance, both capable of racing prominently without leading, could benefit if they find a clean passage as the front-runners tire approaching the final two furlongs. Distant Shore has consistent place form at this trip on Good ground and Radiance brings class from a 326-day absence that could translate well fresh.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is truly brutal and several horses come from well off the pace to mow down the tiring leaders in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends heavily on Big Bear Hug, a genuine hold-up horse with solid AW form, getting a clear run through late, and on Spirit Of Athene and Guesstimate — both redistributed prominent types — finding late gears they would not naturally deploy. Because Spirit Of Athene and Guesstimate are not true hold-up horses, this shape is the least reliable; if it materialises, Big Bear Hug is the only runner genuinely built for it.

watchPoints.text: She Commands, Pomme Pomme, and Asset will all break looking to lead — watch the first two furlongs for a three-way speed duel that could detonate the race's stamina test far earlier than intended.

Rastnet carries 142lbs at the head of the weights but has six AW places from nine starts — if he gets a clean run from a prominent position tracking the pace battle, his finishing kick on this surface is a serious threat to the leaders.

Guesstimate and Spirit Of Athene are both natural prominent horses pushed into midfield or hold-up roles on this pace map — watch for Cieren Fallon and Kieran Shoemark hunting gaps on the rail from the 3f pole where traffic is expected to be at its worst.

Deedaydiva's 94-day absence, unproven AW record, and reliance on softer ground make her a major price risk — if she fails to handle the Standard surface, she could stop suddenly and cause interference for horses coming from behind.

Big Bear Hug is the only genuine hold-up horse in the race — Pat Cosgrave will need a strong pace to maintain to set up his late run, but if that pace materialises as expected, watch where he is positioned turning for home as he is the one runner truly built for a strong-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Dotties Star
runners_data.note: Won at 12f on Standard AW last time and ran well at 16f on soft, so the trip and surface are squarely in her favour; a hold-up runner who will need clear daylight late but has genuine course-relevant form.

runners_data.name: Dubai Immo
runners_data.note: Has modest AW form at this track and a 54-day absence to overcome; a true hold-up runner who will sit at the rear, and in a race with a slow pace this position is likely to prove problematic — tongue-tie applied.

runners_data.name: Fighting Poet
runners_data.note: Blinkered hold-up horse whose recent form figures of -40689 offer little encouragement; only two runs on Standard going in the last 15 make the AW surface a slight concern, and an 8-year-old competing off OR 45 faces stiff questions.

runners_data.name: Foinix
runners_data.note: On a quick five-day turnaround having run just recently; a hold-up type by nature who will be pushed into midfield by the race shape, wearing blinkers, and his recent efforts of 7-7-3 show he can hit the frame but rarely wins.

runners_data.name: Suitcase Smith
runners_data.note: David Egan takes the ride but this 4-year-old's record of -07964 is deeply uninspiring; naturally a hold-up runner compressed into midfield here, and without Standard AW going form to point to, the data offers little support.

runners_data.name: Tiger Beetle
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie and cheekpieces applied, aged 8, and has placed on Standard AW at 10f — the extra distance today is a query; a genuine hold-up runner who has shown the ability to hit the frame when conditions suit.

runners_data.name: Wrist Art
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner, a 9-year-old who wears a tongue-tie and ran only eight days ago; mapped to lead because he is the most likely pace-setter despite being a naturally prominent type — his ability to control the tempo from the front is the defining tactical factor in this race.

runners_data.name: Amalfi Bluebell
runners_data.note: A lightly-weighted 3-year-old carrying 125lbs on a surface where she has managed just one placing from six tries; her hold-up style leaves her at the mercy of the pace shape and her form figures of 577-87 offer no encouragement.

runners_data.name: Charencey
runners_data.note: Has placed twice at 12f on good ground and Billy Loughnane, a high-profile booking, adds appeal; wears tongue-tie and cheekpieces, ran 14 days ago, and a horse who tracks the pace comfortably is ideally positioned to exploit Wrist Art's controlled gallop.

runners_data.name: Crack of Thunder
runners_data.note: Tagged as a fader in the finish and has worrying form figures of 080 with placings in the last four runs; runs off OR 32 — the lowest in the field — and a hold-up runner who fades is the least likely profile to succeed here regardless of the race shape.

runners_data.name: Dinah Myte
runners_data.note: Won at 8f on Standard AW and placed at 10f — the step to 1m4f is an untested stamina query; a hold-up runner who is naturally positioned further back than the race shape allows, but Luke Morris is a quality booking and the horse has strong recent form figures of 761423.

races.paceDynamic: Wrist Art is the sole confirmed pace-setter and will stride into an uncontested lead from flag to finish over this 1m4f Lingfield AW trip, setting a sustainable, controlled tempo that is unlikely to be seriously challenged. The field behind is dominated by hold-up types — Dinah Myte, Suitcase Smith, Foinix, Dubai Immo and others — most of whom will be forced to race closer to the pace than is natural simply because the midfield will compress with no secondary pace to stretch the field. Charencey and Dotties Star, both capable of tracking in midfield-to-prominent positions, are best placed to exploit a controlled pace scenario where a prominent-midfield finisher can produce a sustained late effort rather than a sharp finishing burst. With Wrist Art dictating a gentle gallop unchallenged and the bulk of the field forced into unnatural positions, this race shape strongly favours runners who can sit just off the steady pace and sustain their effort into the straight — a prominent or tracking-midfield profile is the principal beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wrist Art Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Wrist Art dictates a slow-to-moderate solo lead and the field strings out behind without the pace to reel it in.
scenarios.body: Wrist Art sets sail on a comfortable lead and the lack of genuine pace pressure means the gallop is never truly honest, allowing the leader to conserve energy and find again in the straight; runners forced to make ground from the rear are caught cold by the false pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Lands Decisive Blow
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent or close-tracking runner sits just off Wrist Art's controlled pace and produces a sustained run from the home turn to wear it down.
scenarios.body: The steady tempo set by Wrist Art sets up a race where the first horse to challenge from a prominent position has the advantage of a well-judged run without burning stamina reserves; Charencey has placed twice at 12f on good and has the tactical speed to deliver a clean challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Aids Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow that it causes chaos on the home turn and a genuine hold-up horse threads through late.
scenarios.body: A truly crawling tempo can make the race a sprint finish, which would theoretically suit a hold-up runner who gets an unimpeded run, but most of these runners are redistributed from their natural style and lack the sharp finishing burst to capitalise on a sprint-finish scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Suits Stayer
scenarios.trigger: If a pace injection mid-race by one of the compressed midfield runners forces a genuine stamina test over the 1m4f trip.
scenarios.body: A sudden surge in tempo by one of the prominent-running types reshapes the race into an endurance contest, favouring the horse with the deepest reserves at this trip; Dotties Star, who has form at 16f, would be one to benefit if conditions turned genuinely gruelling.

watchPoints.text: Wrist Art sets the entire tactical picture — watch whether Christian Howarth elects to go forward immediately from the stalls or allows others to shape the early pace, as any hesitation could compress the field dangerously.
Charencey's prominent racing style makes him the primary danger to Wrist Art — watch Billy Loughnane's positioning in the first quarter mile to see if he tracks tight to the leader or is forced wide.

Dinah Myte's unproven stamina at 1m4f is a live concern — Luke Morris will need to produce her run at exactly the right moment, and if the pace is slow she risks getting caught in traffic with insufficient room to deliver.

With so many hold-up runners compressed into midfield, the home turn at Lingfield could become congested — watch for scrimmaging and interference between Foinix, Suitcase Smith, Dubai Immo and Amalfi Bluebell as they jostle for position.

Crack of Thunder's fade pattern makes him a horse to monitor for market drifters — if punters are backing him despite his finish-fade flag, it may indicate stable confidence that contradicts the form picture.

races.name: Free Tips On attheraces.com Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Malachy's Wish
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who won at Lingfield (AW) on similar Standard going and on this same trip, giving her a strong course-and-distance profile despite a 59-day absence — she needs cover and a true test to unleash her finishing kick, which this pace shape may not fully supply.

runners_data.name: Three Non Blondes
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner, two wins from seven career starts including a Lingfield AW win on Standard, and Billy Loughnane's claiming experience on a single pace-setter is the key tactical lever — uncontested lead at 7f on this surface is her comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Brisk Symphony
runners_data.note: Shaped well for places on Lingfield AW in similar going (2nd, 7f, Standard), but her true style is hold-up and she is operating out of that role here — Jason Watson will need significant gaps to materialise from what will likely be a genuinely deep position in this compressed field.

runners_data.name: Souffler
runners_data.note: 293 days off the track is an obvious question mark for a horse from a yard whose T14 form is respectable, but her sole win came at Goodwood over 7f on good and she has untested potential — Taryn Langley's 5lb claim softens the weight burden significantly.

runners_data.name: Pints In Peace
runners_data.note: Two wins on this surface (Standard, 7f) make her form profile relevant, but she is a genuine hold-up horse funnelled into a midfield slot on paper — Finley Marsh will likely find her further back than the map implies, and this pace is unlikely to be strong enough to create the gap she needs.

runners_data.name: Bone Marra
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR 86 carrying 136lbs, but has three wins on this course-and-going combination and Ollie Sangster's yard is firing (T14: 3/12) — prominent style and strong AW form make her the most naturally suited profiler to challenge Three Non Blondes.

runners_data.name: Do Bronxs
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who placed on this track at 8f on Standard going but has no wins on the surface; David Egan will ride him patiently from what may be a deep position, and his form figures here suggest a place contender rather than a winner in a shape that doesn't generate strong pace.

races.paceDynamic: Three Non Blondes is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Billy Loughnane can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop down Lingfield's polytrack seven-furlong straight. This is a clean solo-lead scenario: Three Non Blondes sets the fractions, the prominent pair Bone Marra and Souffler will slot in directly behind and keep tabs rather than force a pace battle, creating a steady-to-moderate tempo that compresses the field and limits the advantage for true hold-up horses. The field holds more off-the-pace types than the map can honestly accommodate at the rear — Brisk Symphony and Pints In Peace are natural hold-up horses pushed into midfield positions on the map but both will likely find themselves further back than ideal in practice, reducing their ability to deliver the late surge this shape would require. This race shape emphatically favours the lead-to-prominent profile: a front-runner able to control fractions and a prominent horse with tactical speed to sit just off the pace and kick, rather than closers needing a true pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Challenge
scenarios.trigger: If Three Non Blondes dictates an uncontested, moderate gallop and the race is won from the front or close to it.
scenarios.body: Three Non Blondes controls every yard at a rhythm that suits her, and prominent trackers Bone Marra and Souffler enjoy an energy-efficient trip stalking the leader into the straight. The prominent profile benefits most here — high OR, good course-and-distance form, and the ability to challenge off a slow-moderate pace without needing an injection of pace from behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Bone Marra or Souffler travel smoothly just off the pace and pounce on Three Non Blondes inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Bone Marra has strong course form and a trainer in excellent recent shape (T14: 3/12), and Souffler showed a big win on her form string — both are capable of taking advantage when the leader is collared.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is somehow stronger than expected and a genuine closer gets the gap they need in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This scenario demands that Brisk Symphony or Pints In Peace — both true hold-up types operating out of their natural position — find clear daylight, which is compromised by their redistribution away from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Fades, Upset
scenarios.trigger: If Three Non Blondes overcooks the fractions or is outpaced by a rejuvenated runner returning from a lay-off.
scenarios.body: Souffler returns after 293 days off but showed a win at Goodwood and could outrun a forecast price if fresh; Do Bronxs has placed on this surface and David Egan can manufacture late runs in muddled finishes.

watchPoints.text: Three Non Blondes (Billy Loughnane) sets all the fractions alone — if she controls the tempo to her liking, there is no mechanism in this field to hunt her down before the line.

Bone Marra is top weight at OR 86 but her trainer's T14 strike rate of 3/12 and her strong course-and-going record make her the biggest threat to the leader; watch whether she can close the gap into the straight.

Brisk Symphony and Pints In Peace are genuine hold-up horses likely to race further back than their mapped positions suggest — if neither can secure a wide run in the straight, their chances are effectively neutralised by the race shape.
Souffler reappears after 293 days off the track; a big price is likely and any significant move in the market from Taryn Langley should be noted given her unexposed profile at this trip.

Malachy's Wish's 59-day absence may blunt her sharpness slightly, but her two wins on this surface over this trip in similar conditions (Standard, 7f) make her one to keep onside if the pace quickens late.

runners_data.name: Jackson Street
runners_data.note: Holds a solid AW record at Lingfield and has placed on similar Standard surfaces three times in his last 15 comparable runs; naturally prominent, he should sit just off King David and is well-placed to capitalise if the pace is ordinary.

runners_data.name: Yes Waliim
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes' three-year-old is a genuine hold-up type whose recent form (six runs, no wins on Standard) gives little confidence; seven-furlong AW form is unproven and the 7lb claim from Hoodless may not offset the positional difficulty.

runners_data.name: Distillation
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Standard AW just five days ago which is the most relevant piece of form in the race; a natural hold-up type who must produce a strong late run, but recent fitness and course-relevant experience make him the most credible closer in this field.

runners_data.name: Ashford Hill
runners_data.note: In reality a hold-up performer who will be operating closer to midfield than he prefers in this field of rear-runners; Dominic Ffrench Davis has a quiet recent strike rate and the horse's best AW efforts have come with a bigger field spread — harder to deliver here.

runners_data.name: Gal
runners_data.note: Won over 7f at Goodwood last time and that course-and-distance form translates well in principle; naturally prominent, Hope Regan's 7lb claim keeps the weight competitive, but 28 days off and a below-par AW record (one run, no placing) are mild queries.

runners_data.name: Twitch
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old veteran who wants to race from the rear but will find himself marooned in midfield in this congested back-end; his best 7f AW figures have come when given a strong gallop to close into, which is unlikely with King David in control.

runners_data.name: Aplaceinthesun
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's three-year-old is a confirmed hold-up type pushed forward on the map by congestion at the rear; limited Standard AW form (two runs, no placing) and a modest OR of 49 make it hard to make a case even if he secures a better berth.

runners_data.name: Material Girl
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's filly wears a hood and is a consistent prominent type who has posted a sequence of fair placed efforts on Standard; at OR 45 and stepping up to 7f for the first time, stamina is the unknown but her positioning should be straightforward.

runners_data.name: King David
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Gay Kelleway who has not won in six runs and whose recent form string reads poorly; the style-fit tag acknowledges he is not a natural race-shaper of the highest order, but in this field he should lead comfortably and make every post a winning one.

runners_data.name: Prince Ali
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old with a strong record at 8f (two wins) and a recent placed effort over a mile; stepping back to 7f may not be his optimum but Thomas Faulkner's runner is in decent current form and Zoe Lewis's 7lb claim softens the weight, though hold-up style is a concern at this pace.

runners_data.name: African Spirit
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' five-year-old wears a hood and cheekpieces and has produced his best AW figures in sprinting company (placed twice at 7f Standard); a genuine hold-up performer displaced toward midfield by field congestion — his 7f AW course form is respectable but the positional compromise is real.

races.paceDynamic: King David is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival willing to press him hard for the lead, he should coast into an uncontested, comfortable gallop down the Lingfield AW straight. Jackson Street and Gal are the likeliest horses to sit just off his heels in a prominent berth, giving the pace a modest but consistent tempo on Standard ground. The field is loaded with natural hold-up types — African Spirit, Aplaceinthesun, Ashford Hill, Twitch and Prince Ali all want to race from the rear — but there are more of them than the map can accommodate at the back, meaning several will end up racing closer to midfield than they would prefer, diluting their closing punch. With one rider dictating at a measured pace, the race shape strongly favours horses who can secure a prominent position from early on and travel into the race, rather than those relying on a strong late surge from off a slow gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: King David Dictates Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If King David is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and set a steady, controlled tempo throughout the seven furlongs.
scenarios.body: King David, tagged with a style-fit note at 0.94 suggesting he is racing slightly out of role for pure lead dominance, still commands the race if uncontested; horses who can track him prominently like Jackson Street and Gal are ideally placed to pounce. On Standard AW going at Lingfield where front-runners receive no ground-related penalty, those travelling sweetly in second or third have the clearest route to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Duel It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Jackson Street and Gal push forward assertively and apply enough pressure to King David that the pace quickens into a genuine contest between the first three.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop exposes King David's stamina limits at 7f on the AW and brings the handiest prominent types into a straight fight; Jackson Street's solid similar-going record (12 of 15 runs on comparable surfaces) and Gal's recent Goodwood win give both strong claims. Material Girl, also a prominent type wearing a hood, could pick up pieces if the duel burns out the principals.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Find Enough Momentum
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and horses who managed to get to midfield despite their hold-up instincts produce a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Distillation is the most credible finisher here — a recent 7f AW winner at Standard and only five days since that effort, giving confidence in current form — while Prince Ali has placed multiple times at 8f and his class over further could allow him to stay on. However, most genuine hold-ups have been redistributed closer to midfield than suits them, tempering confidence in a true late flourish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Reshuffling
scenarios.trigger: If there is early jostling for position among the prominent types and several redistributed hold-up horses get shuffled further back than even their mapped position suggests.
scenarios.body: A chaotic early phase could produce an uneven gallop that scrambles the field and opens the race up to an atypical winner; Ashford Hill or African Spirit, both genuine hold-up types forced into unfamiliar mid-pack positions, might benefit if the race suddenly quickens and then eases. This remains a low-probability shape because the field, despite its density of rear-runners, lacks a true pace duel trigger to create the necessary disorder.

watchPoints.text: King David (front-runner, style-fit 0.94) — watch at the start whether Toby Moore (7lb claim) settles him quickly or gets into a battle for lead, as any early pressure would transform the race shape entirely.
Distillation runs just five days after his last outing — monitor in pre-race for any signs of freshness or stiffness that could undermine what is otherwise the most current form in the field.

Multiple hold-up types (African Spirit, Aplaceinthesun, Ashford Hill, Twitch) will all be competing for the same limited rear-midfield ground — watch the first two furlongs for crowding and horses being carried wider than intended.
Gal is 28 days since her last run and has limited Standard AW experience — her Goodwood form is on Good ground, so note her early action on the AW surface to gauge how well she handles the switch.

Prince Ali steps back from 8f to 7f; watch whether Zoe Lewis rides him aggressively to secure a good early position or allows him to settle naturally, as his pattern suggests he needs at least a mile to be at his best.
